Comment on five (5) of the items (a)–(j): (a) “The people of Israel did what was evil in the sight of the Lord.” (Judges 3:7). (4 marks) (b) “Here I am; testify against me before the Lord.” (1 Samuel 12:3). (4 marks) (c) “Your house shall be made desolate.” (1 Kings 13:34). (4 marks) (d) “Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.” (2 Kings 2:11). (4 marks) (e) “The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.” (Isaiah 9:2). (4 marks) (f) “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, before you were born I consecrated you.” (Jeremiah 1:5). (4 marks) (g) “And you, son of man, do not be afraid of them, nor be afraid of their words.” (Ezekiel 2:6). (4 marks) (h) “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.” (Hosea 4:6). (4 marks) (i) “Woe to those who are at ease in Zion.” (Amos 6:1). (4 marks) (j) “Behold, your king is coming to you, righteous and having salvation.” (Zechariah 9:9). (4 marks)
Describe the role of Jephthah as a judge and the controversy of his vow. (20 marks)
Explain the rejection of Saul as king and its lessons for Christian leaders today. (20 marks)
Analyze the reasons for the destruction of Jerusalem in 586 B.C. (20 marks)
Show the teachings of Isaiah on social justice and their relevance today. (20 marks)
Explain Amos’s visions of judgment in chapters 7–9. (20 marks)
Discuss the opposition faced by Jeremiah in his ministry. (20 marks)
Using five examples, explain why Ezekiel is regarded as a prophet of visions. (20 marks)
